_: The SMK-37 page's firmwares (tools/make_fm1.py renders web/smk37.html's <!--SMK-CARDS--> from it). The versions here are the page's fallback: tools/fm1_sync.py reads the live ones every run (genkigenki.github.io/smk37's const FW; "tags": the newest tag of "tags_repo" that matches) into catalog.json, and the page takes them from there. The ports' kinds come from tools/fm1_sync.py (their FM-1 entries).

own.name: Felucca SMK
own.what: Felucca's synthesis and sequencing on the SMK's 37 keys, pads, knobs, faders, wheels and display: engines from FM6 to phase distortion, chiptune and samples, a step sequencer, a browser Studio and a simulator.
own.note: Its installer builds the package from the keyboard's official firmware 016 and its calibration: 016 first, back up before.

own.name: OberVave
own.what: One polyphonic analog-style synth after the classic 8-voice American polys of 1979-84: 32 programs, chorus, delay and plate reverb, an arpeggiator, a two-track step sequencer on the 16 pads, filter and effects on the fader banks.

own.name: Makkuro37
own.what: A microtonal drone synth: eight drones in eight columns, each a little soot creature on the screen, the pads gate them, a CHAOS pad, fader banks, 96 presets in six themes. After the Subharmonicon and the Horn of Abraxas.

own.name: Vector37
own.what: An orbiting overtone synth: four corners of two overtone generators each, a sun on a path and a moon around it decide how much of each you hear. Pads and knobs are the planets, the faders the path; eight sounds, MIDI out on the 3.5 mm jack. After the Beetlecrab Vector.

ports.name: Snoop37
ports.what: SLOOP, the four-track looper groovebox, with the SMK's pads in track colours, a pad sound picker, fader banks and drums on the outer keys.

ports.name: X0X
ports.what: A 909, an 808, two 303s with a line generator and a breakbeat player, all at once; the pads as a 16-step grid.

ports.name: FoMni
ports.what: An Omnichord-style chord harp: the 16 pads become the strum plate, the keybed holds the chords.

ports.name: MAKU
ports.what: An always-on ambience machine: power it on and a new, random, in-key world is already playing; verbs on the buttons and wheels.

ports.name: Rainbow Mode
ports.what: A music toy for kids: colour-coded notes on the pads, 40 friends who sing along, no menus.

ports.name: GHOULBOX
ports.what: Dungeon synth: dark ambient, medieval and fantasy sounds, drones, a hurdy-gurdy crank and two sounds at once.

ports.name: ChoralRoot
ports.what: A chord instrument in the manner of the Orchid: one hand plays roots, the other picks the chord.

ports.name: ORBIT
ports.what: A four-track groovebox with OP-1-inspired screens: three synth parts, a drum machine, an event tape and a mixer.

ports.name: AMB-1
ports.what: A generative ambient machine after Music for Airports: loops of different lengths drift past each other and never repeat.

ports.name: Polly
ports.what: A pocket arranger after the Yamaha QY70: a band of eight General MIDI instruments follows the chords you play.

ports.name: winampFM Synth
ports.what: A synth groovebox in the look of Winamp 2.x, built on SLOOP: player, playlist, effect sliders and a visualizer.
